title: To amend the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 to extend the authorities of title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 through April 30, 2026, and for other purposes.

summary.headline: Short-term extension of foreign intelligence surveillance powers under FISA Title VII, including Section 702, through April 30, 2026.
summary.what_it_does: This law extends the government's surveillance powers under Title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act, which includes Section 702. These powers let US intelligence agencies collect communications of foreign people located outside the United States. The extension runs only through April 30, 2026, about two weeks after the law was signed. The title also says "and for other purposes," but no official summary is available to explain any other provisions.

who_it_affects.group: US intelligence agencies, such as the NSA, FBI, and CIA
who_it_affects.how: They can keep using Title VII surveillance powers without a lapse until April 30, 2026.

who_it_affects.group: Foreign people outside the United States
who_it_affects.how: Their communications can continue to be targeted for collection under these powers during the extension.

who_it_affects.group: Americans who communicate with people overseas
who_it_affects.how: Their messages may still be collected when they communicate with foreign targets, as allowed under the existing program.
They must keep following government orders to help with this collection during the extension.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted April 18, 2026; extends the authorities through April 30, 2026.
